conclusions: The board DCXO is 26 MHz; this is distinct from SMHC3 mux0 SYS_CLK24M. Do not blindly replace the existing 24 MHz module parent by 26 MHz.

The shared SYS_CLK24M source is documented as a DCXO/PLL_REF mux with fixed 24 MHz output. Tina Linux and U-Boot both register sys24M as 24 MHz. No software-selectable SYS_CLK24M mux register was identified in this review.
The next HS candidate should verify PLL_REF from observed registers and the known 26 MHz DCXO, including before low-speed SYS_CLK24M use, rather than use an unvalidated constant.

PERI1 output1 N/P1/input-divider fields and SMHC3 mux3 agree between manual and donor. But the autogen header defines PERI1 CTRL bit24 FREF_SEL, which the manual marks reserved. The draft currently ignores this bit and can decode a direct 26 MHz input as 24 MHz. Require the known REFPLL selection or reject an unresolved source.
Capture PERI1 pattern registers to exclude active sigma-delta modulation before calling the integer decode exact. Nominal register arithmetic is not a physical frequency measurement.

register_model.example_wrong_input: N100,P1=3,input_div1 gives 800 MHz from24 MHz but866.666...MHz from26 MHz. Using the wrong parent would overclock a nominal25/50 MHz plan.

Frequency bucket must follow validated actual card rate. A literal52MHz enters the next bucket and is not the reviewed50MHz step.
required_next_steps: Review and integrate explicit parent checks into a later named candidate.
Read and save actual REF/PERI1/PAT/SMHC3 controls without retuning PLL or rail.
Use staged25MHz then50MHz HS SDR only after matched integrity/error checks.
